references.text: The same introductory formula is used repeatedly in Leviticus, where the Lord speaks to Moses and gives him instructions for the people of Israel.
Same formula where the Lord speaks to Moses to give new laws and regulations.
The preceding context where the Lord continues to speak to Moses about holiness laws for the priests.
"The Lord spoke to Moses" is a recurring formula that confirms that Moses was God's chosen mediator of his will to the people.
The same introductory formula is used in Numbers, showing the continuity of God's revelation to Moses.
Hebrews refers to how God spoke to the fathers through the prophets, including Moses, before he spoke through the Son.
